message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The mane’s development is largely governed by androgen levels (testosterone), and the genetic regulation that allows a male lion to grow a mane is considered a dominant trait—meaning that if a male inherits the allele responsible for mane growth, he will develop a mane regardless of the allele inherited from the other parent.
